:::{#def-integral-nonneg}
<!-- def-equiv-ok: the alternative notation restates the defined integral -->
#### Integral of a non-negative function

Let $(S, \salg, \measure)$ be a [measure space](#def-measure-space),
and let $f : S \to [0, \infty)$ be [measurable](#def-measurable-function).
The **integral** of $f$ with respect to $\measure$ is
[@wikipedia_lebesgue_integration]

$$
\int_S f \, d\measure \eqdef
\sup \set{\sumin \paren{\inf_{s \in A_i} f(s)} \measure(A_i)}
$$

where the [supremum](algebra.qmd#def-supremum) is over all ways
of writing $S$ as the union of finitely many nonempty
[pairwise disjoint](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-pairwise-disjoint) [sets](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/sets.html#def-set) $\dsn{A}$ in $\salg$,
and each $\inf_{s \in A_i} f(s)$ is the [infimum](algebra.qmd#def-infimum)
of the values of $f$ on $A_i$.
In the sums, $0 \cdot \infty \eqdef 0$, and $x \cdot \infty \eqdef \infty$ for $x > 0$;
the supremum is $\infty$ if some sum is $\infty$.
The integral is also written $\int_S f(s) \, d\measure(s)$.

[@billingsley1995probability, Section 15]

:::
